text:
Maria: Heads up — AcmeCorp says the enterprise credit Sales issued (PO-88144) never showed up on their invoice. They tried to apply via the portal and hit a 403. Customer: acct_9876. Can we triage?

Aj: thanks Maria — I got this. Please paste the exact error and any screenshots, will loop Sales Ops.

Maria: repro steps (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/credits/apply 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer USER_TOKEN_XXX\" 
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" 
  -d '{"account_id":"acct_9876","amount":10000,"po_note":"PO-88144"}'

# response:
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "unauthorized: token scope missing: grants:manual"
}
```

ops-bot: billing-service alert: spike of 403s on /credits/apply for tenant acct_9876 at 2025-08-14T12:34:20Z (auto-created incident).

Kevin: I see inbound requests from portal that are missing ledger mapping for po_note. The ledger call rejected because reference_id null. Pulling more logs now.

Maria: screenshot attached (invoice missing promo line). Sales says they added note 'enterprise-contract-2025' on their PO record, but portal backend seems to send `contract_id` instead of `po_note`.

Sam: can repro locally with a sanitized token. Looks like two issues: (1) portal uses user token without grants:manual scope — explains 403; (2) request transform drops po_note when `contract_id` present. Quick test I ran:
```
# sanitized request used to repro
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer SANITIZED_USER\" -d '{"account_id":"acct_9876","contract_id":"enterprise-contract-2025","amount":10000}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/credits/apply
# response 403 + body: {"error":"unauthorized: token scope missing: grants:manual"}
```

Maria: confirmed same on customer's end. They only saw the 403, so portal retried without proper service token, and the mapping never reached billing.

Lucy: For immediate customer satisfaction we should do a manual grant to the ledger and issue a corrected invoice. Runbook steps (internal):
```
# grant via internal CLI (acctops privileged)
redwood-cli credits grant --account acct_9876 --amount 10000 --reason \"Enterprise PO PO-88144\" --po-note \"PO-88144\" --performed-by aj@redwood.com
# then create ledger adjustment and reissue invoice
redwood-cli ledger adjust --account acct_9876 --amount -10000 --reference PO-88144 --comment \"apply sales-issued promo\"
```
Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/credits-manual

Kevin: I'll hold off on the ledger adjustment until the grant is visible and we confirm no double-apply. After grant, I'll post the compensating transaction and reissue invoice.

Aj: I'll notify the customer that we're applying the credit manually and will confirm when invoice updated. @Sam can you scope a short-term fix: ensure portal exchanges a service token for manual grants and passthrough `contract_id -> po_note` mapping? If we can't fully patch before EOD, a small validation on the portal to block user-token paths would avoid more 403s.

Sam: yep. Short plan: add mapping in portal request transform (contract_id -> po_note), validate token scopes on client side and exchange for service account token for `/credits/apply`. Add unit tests. PR opened: #2319, staging deploy in ~1h, then can schedule prod hotfix tonight (~P0->P1 window).

Maria: customer is OK with manual grant today if we can get invoice corrected. Please mark as blocked until grant done.

ops-bot: Created incident INC-2025-73, priority P2, assignee @Sam.

Kevin: Manual grant done (internal tx id tx_55577). I will post confirmation once invoice reissued.

Aj: thanks all — I'll close loop with Sales and the customer once invoice shows the credit. :thumbsup:
